Why Flip stands out

If you film alone, this page is for you. Everyone else can wait.

Most drone pages try to speak to pilots, photographers, travellers and professionals at once — and end up speaking to nobody. This one answers one person's question: “Can I film myself, properly, without a second person holding a camera?”

Simple setup

Simple setup, stunning results

Three steps between the bag and a tracked, level, 4K shot of yourself — most days in under a minute.

1

Unfold the cages

Flip the four guards out. Fully deployed, they power the drone on — unfolding is the on-switch.

2

Launch from your palm

Hold it flat, choose a shooting mode with the mode button, and let it rise off your hand.

3

It follows. You create.

AI tracking keeps you framed while you talk. Wave it back, and it lands on your palm.

Camera

The same sensor class as a Mini 4 Pro. In a drone you can fly at yourself.

A 1/1.3-inch CMOS sensor at f/1.7 shoots 48 MP stills, 4K/60fps HDR and 4K/100fps slow motion, with 10-bit D-Log M for footage you can actually grade. A 3-axis mechanical gimbal keeps every frame level while the drone follows you.

This is not a selfie drone with a toy camera — it is a proper camera that happens to fly itself.

  • 48 MPstills from the 1/1.3-inch sensor
  • 4K/100fpsslow motion for B-roll of your own shots
  • 10-bit D-Log Mflat colour for grading in the edit
  • Dual Native ISO Fusioncleaner low-light pieces to camera
Safety

Four folding cages. Zero exposed propellers.

The Flip's signature is its foldable full-coverage propeller guards — they fold flat for transport, flip out to fly, and power the drone on when fully deployed. That is what makes it flyable close to people, in gardens and courtyards, where an unguarded drone is a liability.

Forward 3D infrared sensing watches what's ahead and brakes automatically — even at night.

The honest part: sensing is forward and downward only — there is no side or rear detection, so the cages, not sensors, are the side protection. Obstacle avoidance also switches off during AI tracking modes, and real-world flight time runs below the 31-minute rating, partly because the guards add drag.
Flight

31 minutes rated. Plan for the real number.

Up to 31 minutes on paper, with DJI O4 holding the live view up to 13 km (FCC) / 8 km (CE). For a solo creator, flight time is takes, not airtime: plan your piece-to-camera and tracking shots around roughly two-thirds of the rating in real flying, and carry a second battery for a full session.

No, not for the basics — palm takeoff and AI tracking modes work without one. A controller gives you full manual flight and the longer-range link.

No — forward 3D infrared and downward vision only. The Flip's answer is physical rather than electronic: full cages around every propeller, so the sides are protected by structure, not sensors.

Rated up to 31 minutes in lab conditions. Real-world active flying runs lower — plan around roughly two-thirds of the rating, and carry a second battery for a full session.

Yes — 2.7K vertical shooting, made for social posting without re-editing the whole clip.

Under 249 g it sits in the sub-250 g class in many countries — but rules differ by country. Check your local rules before you fly; in Nigeria, check NCAA requirements.
